Welcome to the admin panel.

Here you can manage the general settings, the configuration, the interface settings and the hooks.

Start by choosing one of the sections in the sidebar.
admin.description: Configure your network and manage your server.

default.title: Default route
default.description: Where client traffic goes when no rule below matches it.
default.blockWarning: Only traffic matched by a rule will get out. Clients can still reach each other.

dns.title: Domain rules will not match anything yet
dns.explanation: Rules written as domains only work for lookups this server sees. That needs the resolver switched on below, and clients handed this server as their DNS.
dns.afterFix: Only newly downloaded client configs pick this up. Existing devices keep their current resolver until their config is downloaded again.
dns.fixed: New client configs will use this server for DNS
dns.bypassExplanation: These override the default and will keep bypassing domain rules. Change them individually if that is not what you want.
dns.interceptOff: Answering lookups is switched off. Turn it on in the DNS section below.
dns.notListening: Answering lookups is switched on, but the server could not bind port 53: something else in this network namespace holds it. Check the container log.

gateways.title: Gateways
gateways.description: Interfaces traffic can be sent through. A sidecar container joins this network namespace and its interface shows up here.
gateways.name: Name
gateways.noneAvailable: Nothing else found. A VPN container has to run in this container network namespace for its interface to appear here.
gateways.notSuggested: This looks like host or container plumbing rather than a tunnel.
gateways.markTitle: Packet mark and routing table, assigned automatically
gateways.statusOff: Switched off. Rules pointing here fall through to the default action, and a default route through it goes direct
gateways.statusStale: Interface is up, but the far end has not answered for {minutes} min.
gateways.statusNeverAnswered: Interface is up, but the far end has never answered.
gateways.statusBlock: Traffic for this gateway is dropped, not sent elsewhere
gateways.statusDirect: Traffic for this gateway is going direct for now, as configured
gateways.statusFallback: Traffic for this gateway is going through "{name}"
gateways.reconnectTitle: Drop the tunnel's session and open a new one: a fresh handshake, possibly a different far end. Takes a second or two, during which this gateway's traffic goes the way its "if unavailable" setting says.
gateways.reconnectNoAnswer: Reconnected, but the far end has not answered yet
gateways.unavailableTitle: What happens to this gateway's traffic while its interface is gone, down, not answering or cannot carry the address family. Dropping is the safe choice: a rule that says "only through the tunnel" never quietly goes out the open internet. Sending direct suits a default route through a tunnel that sometimes fails, where no tunnel beats no internet. Through another gateway sends it into a fallback; that gateway's own setting decides what happens when it is unavailable too, so gateways chain. A switched-off gateway is unaffected.
gateways.noIpv6Title: This interface has no routable IPv6 address, so IPv6 traffic aimed at it is discarded rather than sent down a tunnel that cannot deliver it. IPv4 is unaffected.

rules.title: Rules
rules.description: Checked top to bottom; the first match decides. Anything unmatched falls through to the default route.
rules.empty: No rules yet, so all traffic follows the default route.
rules.name: Name
rules.patternsHelp: example.com matches that name, *.example.com matches subdomains only, .example.com matches both, *word* matches anywhere, * matches everything
rules.addresses: Addresses and subnets, one per line
rules.addressesHelp: IPv4 or IPv6, with or without a prefix. Use 0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0 to mean all traffic.
rules.autoResolve: Keep domain addresses up to date automatically
rules.clientsHelp: Leave all unchecked for the rule to apply to everyone.
rules.matchedTitle: Destinations currently matched, including ones learned from DNS
rules.deleteDialog: Delete rule {name}? Its domains, addresses and client list are lost.
rules.resolvedWildcards: Nothing to look up: wildcard patterns are learned from client lookups instead.

forwards.title: Port forwarding
forwards.description: Reach a client from outside. Only ports {ports} are published by the container.
forwards.nonePublished: The container publishes no ports (ROUTER_FORWARD_PORTS is empty), so nothing can be forwarded. Existing forwards are kept but not installed until ports are published again.
forwards.name: Name
forwards.deleteDialog: Delete forward {name}? Port {port} stops reaching the client.
forwards.unpublishedTitle: The container does not publish this port right now (ROUTER_FORWARD_PORTS). The forward is kept but not installed, and cannot be reached from outside. Publish the port and recreate the container and it comes back by itself.

dnsSettings.title: DNS
dnsSettings.description: Domain rules work by watching client lookups, so those lookups have to come here.
dnsSettings.intercept: Answer client lookups on this server
dnsSettings.interceptHelp: Turned off, the port is released and domain rules stop learning from client lookups. Rules with "keep addresses up to date" still resolve their domains on a schedule; rules written as plain addresses are unaffected either way.
dnsSettings.upstreamsHelp: Tried in order, first answer wins. Addresses only, since resolving a name here would need a resolver of its own.
dnsSettings.handedOutHelp: This is the default DNS from the general settings: it goes into DNS = of newly downloaded client configs. Devices with a config already installed switch only once the config is downloaded again; clients with their own DNS set are left alone.

unavailable.title: Policy routing is not available on this host
unavailable.explanation: The container needs ipset, iproute2 and the iptables mangle table, and one of them is missing. Nothing configured here takes effect until that is fixed; see the FAQ for the kernel modules involved.

applyFailed.title: The last apply did not fully succeed
applyFailed.explanation: Some routing commands failed, so the kernel may not match what is configured here. Check the container log with DEBUG=Router,CMD for the failing commands.

jMax.label: Junk packet max size (Jmax)
jMax.description: Maximum size of junk packets (1-1280*, recommended: 80, must be > Jmin)

s1.label: Init packet junk size (S1)
s1.description: Init packet junk size (0-1132[1280* - 148 = 1132], recommended: 15-150, S1+56 ≠ S2)

h1.label: Init magic header (H1)
h1.description: Init packet header value or range (X or X-Y, where X<Y. Min 5, max 2147483647. Value or range must not overlap with other headers)

h2.label: Response magic header (H2)
h2.description: Response packet header value or range (X or X-Y, where X<Y. Min 5, max 2147483647. Value or range must not overlap with other headers)

h3.label: Cookie reply magic header (H3)
h3.description: Cookie reply packet header value or range (X or X-Y, where X<Y. Min 5, max 2147483647. Value or range must not overlap with other headers)

h4.label: Transport magic header (H4)
h4.description: Transport packet header value or range (X or X-Y, where X<Y. Min 5, max 2147483647. Value or range must not overlap with other headers)

contentPaddingAddition.label: Content padding addition
contentPaddingAddition.description: Random amount of bytes appended to transport packets before encryption

rekeyAfterTime.label: Rekey after time
rekeyAfterTime.description: Seconds before a session is renegotiated (WireGuard default: 120)

keepaliveTimeout.label: Keepalive timeout
keepaliveTimeout.description: Idle seconds before a keepalive is sent (WireGuard default: 10)

maxHandshakeAttempts.label: Max handshake attempts
maxHandshakeAttempts.description: Handshake attempts before giving up (WireGuard default: 18)

randomTrailers.label: Random trailers
randomTrailers.description: Append a random amount of bytes to handshake packets. Must match on both sides, so it is copied to every client

disableCookies.label: Disable cookies
disableCookies.description: Do not answer handshakes with cookie messages when under load. Only affects this side of the tunnel
